user.title: Connect your Cync account
user.description: Cync LAN controls your devices entirely on your local network at runtime. Your account credentials are only used once, here, to pull down your device list - they are not stored in plain text and are not used again unless you re-run setup.

otp.title: Enter the verification code
otp.description: Cync emailed a one-time verification code to your account email address.

confirm.title: Confirm setup
confirm.description: Found {device_count} device(s) on your Cync account. Continue to finish setup and start the local listener.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Cync
reauth_confirm.description: Cync LAN needs to sign in to your account again - the cached session expired or your password changed.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Factory-default Cync device found
bluetooth_confirm.description: A Cync/Telink device broadcasting its factory-default Bluetooth identity was found nearby - this means it hasn't been added to any Cync account yet. Cync LAN controls devices already on your Cync account and network; it doesn't set up brand-new devices. Add it to your account with the official Cync app first, or see this integration's README for provisioning it directly onto your WiFi network without the Cync app.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Cync cloud API. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.no_devices: No devices were found on this Cync account.

abort.already_configured: This Cync account is already configured. Only one Cync LAN account is supported per Home Assistant instance.
abort.unprovisioned_device_found: This device hasn't been added to a Cync account yet, so there's nothing for Cync LAN to set up - see the previous screen for how to add it.

data.local_port: Local TCP port (devices must be redirected here via DNS)
data.export_refresh_interval: Hours between automatic device-list refreshes (0 to disable)
data.enable_light_groups: Create light group entities for Cync device groups
data.hide_group_members: Hide each group's individual member lights from dashboards
data.enable_experimental: Enable experimental commands (advanced) - adds the experimental_* actions for scenes, schedules, motion-sensor tuning and mesh queries. Their wire format is predicted, not confirmed against real hardware; they may do nothing, or something unintended.
data.capture_unknown_packets: Capture unrecognised packets to a log file (advanced) - writes the raw hex of anything connecting to the local port that isn't a Cync device. Use this to identify an unknown client; it is noisy, and needs a full Home Assistant restart to take effect, not just a reload.
data.indicator_led_as_light: Show the indicator ring as a light instead of separate controls
data.capture_firmware: Download firmware updates for inspection (never installs them)
data.hub_envelope_bare: Use the alternate "bare" hub envelope (experiment) - hub commands (scenes, schedules, automations, groups, hub queries) drop the 7-byte routing block, matching how the phone app builds them. Unproven on our wire. Turn this on only if hub commands do nothing with it off, then report which setting worked. Applies immediately, no restart needed.

motion_sensor_select.title: Edit motion sensor settings
motion_sensor_select.description: Choose which motion or ambient-light sensor to edit.

motion_sensor_wake.title: Wake up {device_name}
motion_sensor_wake.description:
{device_name} appears to be offline right now. Press and hold its off button for 5 seconds to wake the device & make it discoverable. The LED light will turn green.

Make sure your phone/hub is within 40 feet of the device during this process, then select Submit to check again.

motion_sensor_settings.title: Motion sensor settings for {device_name}
motion_sensor_settings.description: {device_name} is online. Choose which sensor to tune and its new settings - this sends the change immediately.

experimental_menu.title: Experimental commands
experimental_menu.description: These send mesh commands whose wire format is predicted rather than confirmed against real hardware. They may do nothing, or something unintended.

exp_push_automation.title: Push an automation to Cync hardware
exp_push_automation.description: The automation keeps working as a normal Home Assistant automation, and also runs natively on the hub - so it still fires if Home Assistant is offline. It must have exactly one time-of-day trigger, at most one day-of-week condition, and only light.turn_on actions that set a colour.

exp_scene_membership.title: Scene membership
exp_scene_membership.description: Capture this device's colour inside an existing Cync scene, or remove it. A scene stores one colour per device; brightness and effects cannot be captured.

exp_group_membership.title: Group membership
exp_group_membership.description: Subscribe or unsubscribe this device to a group's mesh address.

exp_motion_schedule.title: Motion-sensor schedule slot
exp_motion_schedule.description: Write one of the four native schedule slots. Hold the sensor's off button for 5 seconds until the LED turns green first, or the device ignores the write.

exp_multicolor_segments.title: MultiColor segments
exp_multicolor_segments.description: Program up to two segments' position and colour. This is one of three primitives a full custom scheme needs, and this integration does not orchestrate the whole sequence - setting segments alone may not produce a visible change.

error.still_offline: Still offline - hold the off button for 5 seconds until the LED turns green, then try again.
error.no_segments: Give a position or a colour for at least one segment.

abort.no_motion_sensors: No motion or ambient-light sensors were found on this Cync LAN account, or the integration hasn't finished starting yet.
abort.experimental_pushed: Pushed {automation} to the hub as a native Cync Scene and Schedule.
abort.no_scenes_or_devices: This needs at least one Cync scene and one device. Scenes are read from the cloud export - create one in the Cync app first.
abort.no_groups_or_devices: This needs at least one Cync group and one device. Groups are read from the cloud export - create one in the Cync app first.
abort.no_rgb_devices: No colour-capable devices were found on this account.

no_devices_connected.description: No Cync devices have connected to the local listener on port {port} since setup finished. This almost always means the DNS redirection prerequisite isn't actually in place yet, or the affected devices haven't been power-cycled since you set it up (they only do a fresh DNS lookup on boot). experimental_set_indicator_led.name: Set indicator LED (experimental)
experimental_set_indicator_led.description: Confirmed working on real hardware (see docs/mesh_opcodes.md). Kept under the experimental_ service name since it's still a recently-corrected command. Sets a device's small status/indicator LED mode, color, and brightness.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Cync device whose indicator LED to set.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Always on, always off, or normal operation.

color.name: Color
color.description: The indicator LED only supports these 4 colors, not full RGB.

wifi_disconnect_blink.name: Blink on WiFi disconnect
wifi_disconnect_blink.description: Blink the indicator LED when the device loses its WiFi connection.

experimental_set_motion_sensor_settings.name: Set motion/ambient sensor settings (experimental)
experimental_set_motion_sensor_settings.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is predicted, not confirmed against a real packet capture. Tunes a motion or ambient-light sensor's enabled state, sensitivity, and timing. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md. Note: the real Cync app requires physically waking the sensor first (press and hold its off button for 5 seconds - the LED turns green when it's discoverable, and your phone should be within 40 feet) before it accepts settings edits. This isn't a special radio mode - it's the device's ordinary online status, confirmed via decompiled-source research. If this call appears to silently do nothing, the sensor is very likely still asleep - the real app itself silently no-ops this exact command family when its target is offline, rather than erroring.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Cync device with the sensor to tune.

sensor_type.name: Sensor type
sensor_type.description: Which sensor on the device to tune.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Turn the sensor on or off. Leave unset to update sensitivity/timing without changing the enabled state.

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

delay_seconds.name: Delay
delay_seconds.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

deactivation_seconds.name: Deactivation delay
deactivation_seconds.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

experimental_execute_scene.name: Activate a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_execute_scene.description: Experimental — both the outer command byte and the target address are predicted, not confirmed against a real packet capture. Activates a saved Cync Scene (a named multi-device state snapshot configured in the Cync app). Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Scenes are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to activate, as configured in the Cync app (0-255).

experimental_set_group_power.name: Set a group's power (experimental)
experimental_set_group_power.description: Experimental — unlike this integration's other experimental services, the command itself (set_power) is fully confirmed; what's unconfirmed is whether device firmware actually responds to a group address as "the whole group" rather than a single device. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Groups are addressed home-wide via the group's own mesh address, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

group_id.name: Group ID
group_id.description: The group's numeric mesh address (32768-65535) - find it in your exported cync_mesh.yaml/raw_mesh.cync, not a value the Cync app displays directly.

state.name: State
state.description: On or off for every device in the group.

experimental_set_motion_sensor_schedule.name: Set a motion sensor schedule slot (experimental)
experimental_set_motion_sensor_schedule.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is confirmed (same fix already confirmed working on real hardware for the indicator LED service), but the predicted cmd_code and this specific command have not themselves been tested against real hardware. Writes one of a group's 4 fixed motion-sensor schedule slots. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md. Note: the real Cync app requires physically waking the sensor first (press and hold its off button for 5 seconds - the LED turns green when it's discoverable, and your phone should be within 40 feet) before it accepts settings edits. This isn't a special radio mode - it's the device's ordinary online status, confirmed via decompiled-source research. If this call appears to silently do nothing, the sensor is very likely still asleep - the real app itself silently no-ops this exact command family when its target is offline, rather than erroring.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The motion/ambient-light sensor device to write the schedule to.

slot.name: Slot
slot.description: Which of the 4 fixed time-of-day slots to write.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Disabled, occupancy-based, vacancy-based, or simple (time-based only).

cct.name: Color temperature
cct.description: 0 (warmest) to 100 (coolest). Exactly one of Color temperature or RGB color must be set.

rgb.name: RGB color
rgb.description: Exactly one of Color temperature or RGB color must be set.

experimental_delete_scene.name: Delete a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_delete_scene.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is directly confirmed (DeleteSceneHubCommand's own op_code, not the hardcoded-0x8E relay bug), but whether this command's real wire frame even rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed - the app builds it via a structurally different, separately-flagged-deprecated framer. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Scenes are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to delete, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

experimental_delete_schedule.name: Delete a Cync schedule (experimental)
experimental_delete_schedule.description: Experimental — same situation as the delete-scene service: the outer command byte is directly confirmed, but whether this command's real wire frame rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Schedules are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

schedule_id.name: Schedule ID
schedule_id.description: The numeric ID of the schedule to delete, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

experimental_toggle_automation.name: Enable or disable a Cync schedule (experimental)
experimental_toggle_automation.description: Experimental — same situation as the delete-scene/delete-schedule services: the outer command byte is directly confirmed, but whether this command's real wire frame rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Enables or disables a saved Schedule without deleting it. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Schedules are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

schedule_id.name: Schedule ID
schedule_id.description: The numeric ID of the schedule to toggle, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The scene this schedule triggers - the app writes this same field with a different byte width than the delete-scene service, per real app-code inconsistency (0-4294967295).

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether the schedule should be active.

experimental_set_group_membership.name: Set a device's group membership (experimental)
experimental_set_group_membership.description: Experimental — this command is dual-path depending on your device's product family: for the rare Sol/C-Reach family it uses a confirmed real op_code (the trustworthy envelope builder, same as everyday brightness/color commands); for virtually every other real device it instead uses the same 0x8E-relay-bug substitution as several other experimental commands in this integration. Either way the predicted cmd_code has not itself been captured. Adds or removes ONE device to/from a group's mesh address - this changes group membership, not a group's power/state (see Set a group's power). Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The individual device to add to or remove from the group - this command targets one device, not the bridge.

group_id.name: Group ID
group_id.description: The group's numeric mesh address (32768-65535) - find it in your exported cync_mesh.yaml/raw_mesh.cync.

member.name: Member
member.description: On to add the device to the group, off to remove it.

reach_flag.name: Reach mode
reach_flag.description: Normal (full mesh participation) or receive-only. Leave as Normal unless you have a specific reason to change it.

experimental_push_automation_to_hardware.name: Push an automation to Cync hardware (experimental)
experimental_push_automation_to_hardware.description: Experimental — reads an existing HA automation's own trigger/condition/action config and pushes it onto the Cync hub as a native Scene + Schedule (create_scene, add_to_scene, create_schedule, add_automation), so it keeps running even if Home Assistant or your network goes down. Requires the automation to have exactly one plain time trigger ('at:' a fixed HH:MM:SS, no entity/template), at most one day-of-week condition (a Time condition with only 'Days' set, no before/after range), and one or more light.turn_on actions, each targeting a Cync LAN light directly (not a light group) with exactly one color set (rgb_color or color_temp_kelvin) - a Cync Scene entry has no brightness field and can't capture any other action type. The command bytes for create_scene/create_schedule/add_automation are directly confirmed from decompiled app source, but whether their real wire frame (a distinct HDLC/PPP-style framing, not this integration's usual envelope) rides over the same TCP connection cync-lan intercepts at all is UNCONFIRMED - see docs/cync_automations.md. If the hub doesn't respond to the scene or schedule step within 10 seconds, nothing (or a partial, orphaned scene) is left behind; the error message explains what to clean up. Please report success or failure with your device model.

automation_entity_id.name: Automation
automation_entity_id.description: The Home Assistant automation to push - it keeps working as a normal HA automation afterward; this only ALSO copies its trigger/action logic onto the Cync hub itself.

experimental_add_device_to_scene.name: Add a device's color to a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_add_device_to_scene.description: Experimental — adds or updates this device's captured color state within an existing Cync scene (created via the Cync app, or via experimental_push_automation_to_hardware/the underlying create_scene function). Exactly one of cct or rgb must be given - a Cync scene entry has no brightness field, so it always implies "device on, at whatever brightness it was last set to," never a specific captured brightness. Confirmed via decompiled app source (AddDeviceSceneCommand), including the fade option (a coded duration bucket, not raw seconds) - the device fades to this color autonomously whenever the scene fires, using the byte captured here. Reachable standalone so it can be tested against a scene you already have, independent of the automation-push flow. Please report success or failure with your device model.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device whose current color should be captured into the scene.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to add this device to (0-255 - this command truncates to 1 byte, unlike delete_scene's 2-byte/toggle_automation's 4-byte scene_id fields).

cct.name: Color temperature
cct.description: 0-100 (0=warmest, 100=coolest). Mutually exclusive with RGB - give exactly one.

rgb.name: RGB color
rgb.description: Mutually exclusive with color temperature - give exactly one.

fade.name: Fade
fade.description: How gradually the device transitions to this color when the scene fires. Leave as "No fade" unless you have a specific reason to change it.

experimental_remove_device_from_scene.name: Remove a device from a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_remove_device_from_scene.description: Experimental — removes this device's captured state from an existing Cync scene, without deleting the scene itself or affecting its other member devices. Unlike most commands in this integration, both device product-family code paths are confirmed from decompiled app source (RemoveDeviceSceneCommand) - there's no unconfirmed format being guessed at here, only the predicted outer command length. Please report success or failure with your device model.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device to remove from the scene.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to remove this device from (0-255).

experimental_set_multicolor_gradient_mod.name: Set MultiColor gradient mode (experimental)
experimental_set_multicolor_gradient_mod.description: Experimental — toggles gradient mode for a custom MultiColor scheme (per-segment RGB programming for segmented/dynamic light strips - a separate, bigger feature from the factory light-effect presets). This is one of 3 confirmed wire primitives for programming a custom scheme (see experimental_set_multicolor_segment_count/experimental_set_multicolor_segments for the other two) - this integration does not orchestrate the full multi-step sequence a real custom scheme needs, only these 3 confirmed primitives are exposed. Confirmed via decompiled app source (SetMultiColorSegmentsCommand); the predicted outer command length is what's unconfirmed. Please report success or failure with your device model.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light strip / segmented device to set gradient mode on.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether gradient mode should be on.

experimental_set_multicolor_segment_coun.name: Set MultiColor segment count (experimental)
experimental_set_multicolor_segment_coun.description: Experimental — sets the total logical segment count for a custom MultiColor scheme - see experimental_set_multicolor_gradient_mode's description for the overall multi-step-sequence context this shares. Confirmed via decompiled app source (SetMultiColorSegmentsCommand); the predicted outer command length is what's unconfirmed, along with the real app's own upper bound for this value (not visible in the decompiled source). Please report success or failure with your device model.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light strip / segmented device to set the segment count on.

count.name: Segment count
count.description: Total number of logical segments (0-255 - no narrower confirmed bound).

experimental_set_multicolor_segments.name: Set MultiColor segment position/color (experimental)
experimental_set_multicolor_segments.description: Experimental — sets up to 2 segments' position and/or color in one command, for a custom MultiColor scheme - see experimental_set_multicolor_gradient_mode's description for the overall multi-step-sequence context this shares. Position and color are independently optional per segment (confirmed directly from the app's own data model, not assumed) - give either, both, or neither per segment slot. At least one of the two segment slots must be given. Confirmed via decompiled app source (SetMultiColorSegmentsCommand); the predicted outer command length is what's unconfirmed. Please report success or failure with your device model.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light strip / segmented device to set segments on.

segment_1_position.name: Segment 1 position
segment_1_position.description: Which physical segment (1-120) this slot addresses. Leave blank to send the "unset position" sentinel.

segment_1_rgb.name: Segment 1 color
segment_1_rgb.description: This segment's color. Leave blank to send "no color" (0,0,0).

segment_2_position.name: Segment 2 position
segment_2_position.description: Which physical segment (1-120) this slot addresses. Leave blank to send the "unset position" sentinel.

segment_2_rgb.name: Segment 2 color
segment_2_rgb.description: This segment's color. Leave blank to send "no color" (0,0,0).

experimental_query_mesh_credentials.name: Experimental: query mesh credentials
experimental_query_mesh_credentials.description: Asks a connected hub for the BTLE mesh name and password. These are what cync-lan-ble-provision needs to add a new device to your EXISTING mesh instead of only a factory-default one. Returns them as action response data - the password is your mesh's shared secret, so treat the response accordingly. EXPERIMENTAL: the response channel is unconfirmed and may simply time out on your hardware.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: The 'Cync LAN Bridge' device, not an individual light.
